raw.thesis:
Narma is creating an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies to address the significant challenges they face in deploying AI automation at scale. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an Observe layer with desktop sensors to capture work patterns, an Intelligence layer ("Brain") to detect employee intent and business value of tasks, and an Execution layer ("Agent Factory") that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents. This system focuses on analyzing the "Work Graph" to identify areas where AI can provide assistance, rather than building new foundation models. The venture aims to provide a single system that observes work, decides on AI actions, and continuously builds agents for "Continuous AI lift."

This venture is for AI-first companies that are struggling to effectively implement AI automation. Specifically, the target user is an enterprise that is experiencing a lack of telemetry to pinpoint AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements for AI initiatives, and constant "drift" in their systems and human resources, hindering their efforts to scale AI. The problem is severe because it directly impacts the ability of AI-first companies to realize the promised benefits and ROI of their AI investments, leading to wasted resources and stagnation in automation efforts.

While not explicitly stated, the venture's focus on "AI-first companies" and addressing issues of "scale" and "Continuous AI lift" suggests a growth startup goal, aiming for significant market penetration and expansion within the enterprise AI sector. The founder is currently at the idea stage, as no artifacts or signals of development or traction are mentioned.

Narma positions itself as a complement to existing AI solutions by leveraging existing foundation models rather than replacing them. It precedes the full-scale deployment of AI by providing the intelligence and automated agent creation necessary to ensure effective and measurable AI automation. It seeks to fill a gap in the value chain where companies struggle to bridge the intelligence-to-execution gap in AI operations.

raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale. It has a three-layered architecture: an Observe layer (lightweight desktop sensors capturing work patterns), an Intelligence Layer (a "Brain" detecting employee intent and business value of tasks), and an Execution Layer (an "Agent Factory" that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents). The system uses existing foundation models and focuses on the "Work Graph" to identify where AI can assist work mid-flow.
